newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels overrun Kisangani airport.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels overrun Kisangani airport.

text.p: Rebels overran the international airport in Zaire's third city of Kisangani after hours of heavy fighting and retreating Zairean soldiers began looting the city, diplomats and aid workers said on Saturday.
"The international airport has already been taken and looting has spread across the city," a senior U.N. official said in Zaire's capital Kinshasa. The fighting began on Friday evening.

A Defence Ministry spokesman in Kinshasa was unable to give details but confirmed there had been shooting. "The situation is very tense and there is movement in every direction," the spokesman told Reuters.

Kisangani, a provincial capital and port dominating the Zaire River which flows west to Kinshasa, is the nerve centre of army operations in the east. The government had concentrated soldiers, Serb mercenaries and Rwandan Hutu allies there.
Aid workers in Kinshasa who were in contact with Kisangani overnight said the fighting started with heavy mortar fire on the northeast outskirts on Friday evening.
Government troops and allied mercenaries had concentrated around the international airport, where military hardware including combat helicopters was based.
"The mercenaries fled the airport but nobody knows where they have gone. Some of the senior military seem to have gone across the river," senior Western diplomat said on Saturday.

Diplomats, aid workers and Western security sources reported shooting in Kisangani itself overnight although it was unclear whether the ill-disciplined Zairean forces were fighting among themselves, looting or resisting the rebels.
Relief agencies and embassies were looking at ways to evacuate foreign nationals from the city, diplomats and aid sources said.

The Tutsi-led rebels took up arms in October vowing to topple veteran President Mobutu Sese Seko. Mobutu has been out of the country for most of the time since August when he had prostate cancer surgery in Europe.
Zaire accuses neighbouring Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi of invading in support of the rebels. All three deny the charge.
